mode_evidence: Mandalabrahmana describes colours 'seen' at set distances before the nose with eyes fully open, streaks of light at the corners of the eyes while looking at space, and a graded sight with closed, half-open and fully open eyes; Sambhavi occurs while 'the physical eyes are seeing externally without winking'.
onset_evidence: Gives three lakshyas as procedures: close ears with forefingers, fix mind on the booming sound, blue light between the eyes and in the heart; look at external space at 4 to 12 digits before the nose and moving the eyes see streaks of light at the corners, after which vision steadies; or practise fully opened-eye gaze at the nose tip, first deep darkness at the palate root, then a sphere of light. No time scales; 'the great science concealed in all the tantras'; a guru's words referenced elsewhere.

conditions.posture: Neck and body erect, mouth closed.
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Fully open eyes aimed at the nose tip (purnima); eyes moved while looking at space; ears closed with forefinger tips for the internal lakshya.
conditions.prerequisites: Taraka yoga practised with introvision accompanied by manas.
conditions.other: Prana and Apana united and kumbhaka for the western light.

stages.label: signs of Sambhavi (purva)
stages.description: Seen in order: a star, a dazzling diamond, the sphere of the full moon, the brightness of nine gems, the midday sun, a flame of fire.

stages.label: uttara (western) light
stages.description: Lustres of crystal, smoke, bindu, nada, kala, star, firefly, lamp, eye, gold, and nine gems.

what_to_do_with_light: Fix the gaze and let the light-sequence unfold; behold the endless sphere of light as Brahman; absorb mind in the bliss it gives.
interpretation: The taraka light is Brahman, the Sachchidananda; Brahma-tejas, the spiritual effulgence.
practice_summary: The Mandalabrahmana Upanishad gives three targets. Internal: close the ears with the tips of the forefingers, fix the mind on the booming sound, and a blue light is seen between the eyes and in the heart. External: look into space before the nose and one sees at 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 digits successively blue space, indigo-black, a red wave, then yellow tones; looking at space while moving the eyes, streaks of light show at the eye corners and vision becomes steady; a light 12 digits above the head brings the nectar state. Brahmana II says to practise with fully open eyes aimed at the nose tip: first a deep darkness at the palate root, then an endless sphere of light. Signs come in order: star, diamond, full moon, nine gems, midday sun, flame.

key_passages.locator: Mandalabrahmana Upanishad, Brahmana I, source lines 11560-11786
key_passages.anchor: When the two ears are closed by the tips of the forefingers, a phatkara
key_passages.paraphrase: With ears closed by the forefingers a booming sound is heard; fixing the mind on it, a blue light is seen between the eyes and in the heart.
key_passages.quote: When the two ears are closed by the tips of the forefingers, a phatkara (or booming) sound is heard. When the mind is fixed on it, it sees a blue light between the eyes as also in the heart.

key_passages.locator: Mandalabrahmana Upanishad, Brahmana I, source lines 11560-11786
key_passages.anchor: When one looks at the external space, moving
key_passages.paraphrase: Moving the eyes while looking at space, streaks of light appear at the eye corners, after which vision can be made steady.
key_passages.quote: When one looks at the external space, moving the eyes and sees streaks of light at the corners of his eyes, then his vision can be made steady.

key_passages.locator: Mandalabrahmana Upanishad, Brahmana II, source lines 11560-11786
key_passages.anchor: That with half opened eyes is pratipat
key_passages.paraphrase: Three sights by eye aperture; the fully open-eyed purnima gaze aimed at the nose tip is to be used.
key_passages.quote: The sight of ama is the one (seen) with closed eyes. That with half opened eyes is pratipat; while that with fully opened eyes is purnima. Of these, the practice of purnima should be resorted to. Its lakshya (or aim) is the tip of the nose.

key_passages.locator: Mandalabrahmana Upanishad, Brahmana II, source lines 11560-11786
key_passages.anchor: seen like a star; then a reflecting (or dazzling) diamond
key_passages.paraphrase: Signs of progress appear in order from star to diamond, full moon, nine gems, midday sun, flame.
key_passages.quote: first it is seen like a star; then a reflecting (or dazzling) diamond; then the sphere of full moon; then the sphere of the brightness of nine gems; then the sphere of the midday sun; then the sphere of the flame of agni (fire); all these are seen in order.
